sections.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.court: Judicial Magistrate First Class (Magistrate) under the PWDVA, on an application under PWDVA s.12. The graph picks this court — never ask the user to pick the court.
sections.escalate_rule: Escalate to human/LLM if: confidence is low, OR any of these facts is missing — who owns the house (husband / in-laws / joint family / rented), who currently lives there (wife, daughter, husband, in-laws), whether she has already been thrown out or is only threatened, the nature of the threats (verbal eviction threat vs. physical removal vs. lock-out), or whether any physical violence has occurred. Do NOT guess ownership or occupancy; do NOT answer on an assumed 'tenancy' basis.
exclusions: Does NOT create ownership, title, or a property share in the house — it is a right to reside only
Does NOT create tenancy rights — NEVER call it 'tenancy rights'; the woman is not a tenant and no landlord-tenant relationship is created
Does NOT by itself stop violence or award money — that needs PWDVA s.18 (protection) and s.20 (monetary reliefs)
Does NOT by itself restrain the respondent from entering or order his removal — that needs a residence order under PWDVA s.19
Not for a woman with no domestic relationship with the respondent, and not for a house that was never a shared household

laya_question.expected_answer_for_test_case: Yes — she lives there with him/his family and faces eviction threats (wife and 8-year-old daughter live in the house in the husband's name; eviction threatened)
options: Yes — she lives there with him/his family and faces eviction threats
Yes — she lived there but has already been thrown out
No — she never lived in that house
Unclear — who lives there / who owns it is not stated
laya_question.question: Does the woman live (or has she lived) in the house with the husband in a domestic relationship, and is she now being threatened with eviction from it?
laya_question.scoring_note: Option 1 or 2 both trigger PWDVA s.17; option 2 additionally strengthens the s.19 claim (restoration of possession). Option 3 excludes s.17. Option 4 escalates for missing facts.

sections.precedent: Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja (2020) — shared household / residence ONLY. The Supreme Court held the right to reside in a shared household is not confined to a house owned by the husband; it extends to a house owned by in-laws/joint family where the woman lived in a domestic relationship. Cite ONLY for residence/shared household — never for custody, never for maintenance, never for Stridhan.
prerequisites: Aggrieved person is a woman in a domestic relationship (here: wife in a Hindu marriage since 2012)
A shared household exists or existed — a household where she lives or has lived with the respondent in a domestic relationship (here: the matrimonial home where she and her daughter live)
Domestic violence alleged or apprehended (here: eviction threats; economic/emotional abuse in the form of withholding maintenance and threatening homelessness)
related_sections: PWDVA s.18 — protection order to stop the threats/violence backing the eviction
PWDVA s.19 — residence order giving the s.17 right enforceable teeth (restraint on dispossession, removal of respondent, alternative accommodation)
PWDVA s.20 — monetary reliefs: maintenance and compensation for expenses/losses arising from domestic violence, including rent for alternative accommodation if she cannot stay
BNSS s.144 (old CrPC s.125) — maintenance for wife and child, parallel to PWDVA s.20
HMA s.24 — interim maintenance pendente lite
HMA s.25 — permanent alimony and maintenance
HMA s.26 — custody of the 8-year-old daughter, who lives in the same shared household
HMA s.27 — Stridhan/property disposal
BNS s.316 (IPC s.406 equivalent) — criminal breach of trust for Stridhan withheld by husband's family
sections.relief: Declaration/recognition of the right to reside in the shared household; the respondent cannot evict, dispossess, or exclude her except in accordance with law. This is the legal foundation — the enforceable orders (restraint on dispossession, removal, alternative accommodation) are obtained under PWDVA s.19.
sections.title: Right to reside in a shared household
sections.when_used: The aggrieved woman is being threatened with eviction, dispossession, or exclusion from the household where she lives or has lived in a domestic relationship, OR she needs the legal basis to remain living there. Triggers on the exact test-case facts: wife and 8-year-old daughter live in a house in the husband's name; husband/his family threaten eviction; she seeks to stay. The right exists whether or not she has any title, ownership, or tenancy in the house, and whether or not the house is in the husband's name, a joint-family property, or owned by in-laws.

sections.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.court: Judicial Magistrate First Class (Magistrate) under the PWDVA, on an application under PWDVA s.12. The graph picks this court — never ask the user to pick the court.
sections.escalate_rule: Escalate to human/LLM if: confidence is low, OR any of these facts is missing — the nature of the threats (words used, who made them, when), whether any physical violence occurred (what, when, injuries, medical/police record), whether the daughter was threatened or harmed, or whether there is an immediate safety risk requiring urgent/ex parte relief. If immediate danger is indicated, flag urgency — do not delay on a routine track. Do NOT minimise threats as 'only a family dispute'.
exclusions: Does NOT by itself grant a right to stay in the house — that is PWDVA s.17, enforced by s.19
Does NOT by itself order the respondent out of the house or restrain his entry — that is PWDVA s.19
Does NOT award money — that is PWDVA s.20 (and BNSS s.144 / HMA ss.24-25 for maintenance)
Does NOT decide custody — that is HMA s.26 / Guardians and Wards Act / HMGA s.6
Does NOT decide Stridhan — that is HMA s.27 / BNS s.316
Not for past violence with no continuing threat or apprehension and no relief sought — the order is forward-looking protection

laya_question.expected_answer_for_test_case: Yes — threats/intimidation/violence are happening or credibly threatened (eviction threats against the wife living in the house; ongoing intimidation while maintenance is withheld)
options: Yes — threats/intimidation/violence are happening or credibly threatened
No — there are no threats or violence, only a property/eviction dispute with no intimidation
Only past violence, no current threat
Unclear — the nature of the threats or any violence is not stated
laya_question.question: Has the husband (or his family) threatened, harassed, intimidated, or used violence against the woman — including threats to throw her out — and is she afraid it will happen again?
laya_question.scoring_note: Option 1 triggers PWDVA s.18. Option 2 routes to s.17/s.19 only. Option 3 needs the date/nature of past violence before deciding. Option 4 escalates for missing facts.

sections.precedent: No case-law precedent relied on for this section in this lane. Do NOT cite Rajnesh v. Neha here (maintenance only) and do NOT cite Satish Chander Ahuja here (residence/shared household only).
prerequisites: Aggrieved woman in a domestic relationship with the respondent
Prima facie domestic violence, or a threat/apprehension of it (eviction threats, harassment, intimidation qualify)
Application under PWDVA s.12 before the Magistrate, supported by a domestic incident report / affidavit as applicable
related_sections: PWDVA s.17 — right to reside in the shared household (the home the protection order defends)
PWDVA s.19 — residence order (removal/restraint directions that a protection order alone cannot give)
PWDVA s.20 — monetary reliefs for losses/expenses caused by the violence
BNSS s.144 (old CrPC s.125) — maintenance
HMA s.24 — interim maintenance pendente lite
HMA s.25 — permanent alimony and maintenance
HMA s.26 — custody of the 8-year-old daughter
HMA s.27 — Stridhan return
BNS s.316 (IPC s.406 equivalent) — criminal breach of trust for Stridhan
sections.relief: Order prohibiting the respondent from committing any act of domestic violence, aiding/abetting it, entering the woman's place of employment or other specified places, communicating with her in specified ways, or committing any other act specified in the order; breach is punishable. It stops the threats; it does not settle residence, money, custody, or property.
sections.title: Protection order
sections.when_used: The respondent has committed, or threatens to commit, an act of domestic violence — including physical violence, threats, intimidation, harassment, or coercion — and an order is needed prohibiting him from doing it. Test-case trigger: eviction threats against the wife (and the pressure this puts on her and the 8-year-old daughter) as a form of domestic violence; also covers any accompanying abuse, harassment, or intimidation by the husband or his family. A protection order is the immediate shield; it operates alongside, not instead of, the residence right (s.17) and residence order (s.19).

sections.escalate_rule: Escalate to human/LLM if: confidence is low, OR any of these facts is missing — who owns the house (husband / in-laws / joint family / rented), who currently lives there, whether she has already been thrown out or is only threatened, whether staying is safe for her and the daughter, or what she actually wants (stay vs. removal vs. alternative accommodation). Do NOT assume removal or alternative accommodation; do NOT promise removal. Do NOT guess ownership.
exclusions: Does NOT decide ownership or title, and does NOT grant a property share — it regulates possession/residence only
Does NOT create tenancy rights — NEVER call it 'tenancy rights'
Does NOT by itself stop violence — that is PWDVA s.18
Does NOT award maintenance or compensation — that is PWDVA s.20 / BNSS s.144 / HMA ss.24-25
Does NOT decide custody — that is HMA s.26 / Guardians and Wards Act / HMGA s.6
Does NOT decide Stridhan — that is HMA s.27 / BNS s.316
Removal of the respondent is not automatic — the Magistrate weighs the facts; do not promise it

laya_question.scoring_note: Option 1 is the test-case answer and the minimum s.19 direction. Options 2-4 are valid s.19 directions on different facts — do not default to them. Option 5 escalates for missing facts.

sections.precedent: Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja (2020) — shared household / residence ONLY. The Supreme Court's broad reading of 'shared household' (including a house owned by in-laws/joint family) is what makes a s.19 residence order available even where the house is not in the husband's sole name. Cite ONLY for residence/shared household — never for custody, never for maintenance, never for Stridhan.
prerequisites: PWDVA s.17 right to reside established — a shared household and a domestic relationship (here: matrimonial home, wife and daughter resident)
Domestic violence alleged or apprehended, or a real risk of dispossession (here: eviction threats)

Application under PWDVA s.12 before the Magistrate; the specific direction sought must be identified (restraint on dispossession vs. removal vs. alternative accommodation) — they are different orders, not one blanket order
related_sections: PWDVA s.17 — right to reside in the shared household (the right s.19 enforces)
PWDVA s.18 — protection order to stop the threats/violence behind the eviction
PWDVA s.20 — monetary reliefs, including rent for alternative accommodation if she cannot stay in the shared household
BNSS s.144 (old CrPC s.125) — maintenance for wife and child

sections.relief: Residence order: restraining the respondent from dispossessing/disturbing her possession of the shared household; restraining the respondent or his relatives from entering it; directing removal of the respondent; restraining alienation/disposal/encumbrance of the shared household; or directing the respondent to secure alternative accommodation of the same level, or pay rent for it, if she cannot reside there. The exact direction depends on the facts — restraint on dispossession is the test-case minimum; removal and alternative accommodation are fact-dependent.
sections.title: Residence order
sections.when_used: The s.17 right to reside needs an enforceable order: restraining the respondent from dispossessing or disturbing the woman's possession of the shared household, restraining him or his relatives from entering it, directing his removal from it, restraining him from alienating/disposing of it or encumbering it, or directing alternative accommodation / rent where she cannot live there. Test-case trigger: eviction threats from the house in the husband's name where the wife and 8-year-old daughter live — the order that makes 'she may stay' enforceable, and the fallback (alternative accommodation or rent) if staying becomes impossible.

sections.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
sections.court: Judicial Magistrate First Class (Magistrate) under the PWDVA, on an application under PWDVA s.12. The graph picks this court — never ask the user to pick the court. Cross-link: maintenance may also be sought under BNSS s.144 / HMA ss.24-25 in the appropriate forum; the graph must not double-count the same maintenance under two heads.
sections.escalate_rule: Escalate to human/LLM if: confidence is low, OR any of these facts is missing — the husband's income (stated Rs 40,000/month in the test case; verify if unstated), what maintenance if any he pays, the woman's and child's monthly needs, whether she needs rent/alternative accommodation, or any specific expenses/losses. Cross-link to Lane 1 for the maintenance figure; do NOT invent an amount here. Do NOT double-count maintenance under both s.20 and BNSS s.144/HMA ss.24-25.
exclusions: Does NOT replace or duplicate a maintenance computation — BNSS s.144 and HMA ss.24-25 are the maintenance provisions; s.20 is the DV Act's monetary-relief route and must be coordinated with them, not double-counted
Does NOT decide custody — HMA s.26 / Guardians and Wards Act / HMGA s.6
Does NOT decide Stridhan return — HMA s.27 / BNS s.316 (Rs 5 lakh gold + Rs 2 lakh cash is Stridhan, not s.20 monetary relief)
Does NOT decide residence/possession — ss.17-19 do that; s.20 covers the money, including rent if she cannot stay
Does NOT decide divorce — HMA ss.13/13B only if divorce is asked for, which it is not here

sections.relief: Monetary relief: maintenance for the woman and child, compensation for expenses and losses caused by domestic violence (including medical expenses, loss of earnings, loss/damage to property), and rent for alternative accommodation where she cannot reside in the shared household. Amount assessed on the husband's income (Rs 40,000/month) and the needs of the wife and daughter; no fixed figure is stated here — Lane 1 owns the maintenance figure.
sections.title: Monetary reliefs
triggers: money for her and the child
sections.when_used: Defined in this lane for its residence/monetary-relief face: the woman has suffered economic loss or expense because of domestic violence — including loss of earnings, medical expenses, loss/damage to property, and rent for alternative accommodation where she cannot live in the shared household — and needs money to meet those expenses and maintain herself and her child. Test-case trigger: husband (Rs 40,000/month) pays no maintenance for two years while threatening eviction; monetary relief under s.20 runs alongside the residence claim (ss.17-19) so that the right to stay is not defeated by cutting off money, and covers rent if she is forced out. Shared with Lane 1 (maintenance) — this lane defines it only for its residence/monetary-relief intersection; Lane 1 owns the maintenance computation.
